questions.question: A researcher wants to compare the median satisfaction scores across four independent groups of users. The satisfaction scores are measured on an ordinal scale, and the data within groups are non-normally distributed. Which non-parametric statistical test is most appropriate for this analysis?

In a simple logistic regression model ln(p / (1 - p)) = b0 + b1 * X, the estimated slope coefficient is b1 = 0.693. Given that e^(0.693) is approximately 2.0, what is the correct interpretation of this coefficient?
options: For a one-unit increase in X, the odds of the event occurring double.
For a one-unit increase in X, the probability of the event increases by 0.693.
For a one-unit increase in X, the probability of the event doubles.
For a one-unit increase in X, the odds of the event increase by 69.3%.

questions.question: An estimator for an unknown population parameter has a bias of 3 and a variance of 16. What is the Mean Squared Error (MSE) of this estimator?

A quality control inspector tests manufactured items sequentially until finding r = 3 defective items. The probability of any single item being defective is p = 0.20, and the test results are independent. Using the Negative Binomial distribution, what is the expected number of non-defective items inspected before finding the 3rd defective item?

In a 2x2 contingency table examining disease status (Present/Absent) versus exposure status (Exposed/Unexposed), 40 exposed individuals have the disease while 10 do not. Among 50 unexposed individuals, 10 have the disease while 40 do not. What is the sample odds ratio of disease comparing the exposed group to the unexposed group?
